Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

ejus

pronoun: genitive of is (feminine as masculine) · Wiktionary

her (someone else’s); his (someone else’s); its (of something else)

In this lexicon

  • her

    the recommended word · classical · Gell. 1.23.7: animum ejus ad inquīrendum everberat

  • his

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 1.9.5: paedagōgum ejus percussit; Cic. Sen. 31: ex ejus linguā melle dulcior fluēbat ōrātiō

  • its

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 124.16: cum ad initium ejus admōtus est; Traupman 335

  • ejus modī: a man of

    classical

  • ejus modī (hujus modī): kind

    classical

  • ejus modī (hujus modī): such

    classical

Notes

  1. 1Write consonantal i as j in all Latin, quotations included: jam, ejus, major, conjungō, Jōannēs. Ruling: Consonantal i is written j.

Examples

  • mulier fit audiendī cupidior; sēcrētum reī et silentium puerī animum ejus ad inquīrendum everberat

    The woman grows more eager to hear; the secret and the boy’s silence goad her mind to find out.Gell. 1.23.7
